title: Forces
standard_text: A force is a push or a pull, measured in newtons; contact forces (friction, applied force) and field forces (gravitational, magnetic, electrostatic). Forces can change the shape, speed and direction of objects; balanced and unbalanced forces; weight and mass. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 9, Energy and Change: Forces)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): contact and field forces, measuring forces, friction, weight and mass, and balanced and unbalanced forces. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

A force is a push or a pull, measured in newtons (N) with a spring balance. Contact forces act when objects touch (friction, tension, applied force). Field forces act at a distance (gravity, magnetic and electrostatic forces).

Weight is the force of gravity on a mass: W = mg, with g = 9,8 N·kg⁻¹ on Earth. Balanced forces cancel out, so the motion does not change; unbalanced forces make an object speed up, slow down or change direction.

Example

Is magnetism a contact force or a field force?

Magnets act without touching.

Answer: a field force

Example

What is the weight of a 10 kg bag on Earth?

W = mg

Answer: 98 N

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up mass (kg) and weight (N).
  • Thinking a moving object needs a force to keep moving.
  • Thinking gravity only acts on falling objects.

items.q: Is this a contact force or a non-contact force: friction between shoes and the floor?
c: a non-contact force (it acts at a distance)
items.e: Most forces need things to touch. Magnetism and gravity act at a distance.
